title: Forgive and have mercy
hook: my Lord, forgive and have mercy, You are the best of the merciful (23:118)

segments.voice: Yesterday, clay, drop, clot, bone, flesh, and your line was blessed is the best creator. What part of you did you catch working? Day four hundred ninety-one.

Some books save the best line for the last page. Surah Al-Mu'minun does something like that. It opened, two days ago, with a bright promise: successful are the believers. Near its end, it goes somewhere dark. People who have died call out, my Lord, send me back, so that I might do right in what I left behind. And they're told it's only a word they're saying. Then the surah gathers itself and closes. Its very last verse is a short prayer, handed to the Prophet ﷺ to say. Today, that last line.

Verse one hundred eighteen. Pickthall: "And (O Muhammad) say: My Lord! Forgive and have mercy, for Thou art Best of all who show mercy." In Arabic: rabbi ghfir warham, wa anta khayru r-rahimin. Two verbs, ighfir and irham. Forgive, and have mercy. They aren't the same request. Ghafara has a sense of covering, of putting something over a fault so it no longer stands exposed. Rahma, mercy, is wider. It's the root of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim in the bismillah, and many scholars connect it to rahim, the womb: care that surrounds you before you've done anything to earn it. So the prayer asks for two things. Cover what I've done wrong. And hold me anyway. Then it gives the reason: You are the best of those who show mercy. Remember Ayyub, nine days ago, calling God the most merciful of the merciful. Different surah, close to the same title. And look where the line sits. Right after the people who begged to be sent back. They asked for a second chance after it was too late. This verse is the version you say while there's still time. And the surah's bookends are worth noticing. It begins, qad aflaha l-mu'minun, successful are the believers. Just before this prayer, it says the deniers will not be successful, la yuflihu. Success at the start, the lack of it near the end, and between them, one short sentence anyone can carry.
screen: `RABBI GHFIR WARHAM.` · `COVER IT, AND HOLD ME ANYWAY.` · `SAID WHILE THERE'S STILL TIME.` · `SUCCESS AT BOTH ENDS OF THE SURAH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: say it ten times. Sit, and let the breath settle. If you pray, say the line slowly, ten times, in Arabic or English: my Lord, forgive and have mercy, You are the best of the merciful. Count on your fingers if that helps. If you don't pray, let ten breaths go by, and on each one think of something you'd like covered, and someone you'd like to be held. The bell holds the time.
Rahma. Mercy, wider than forgiveness: the last verse of Al-Mu'minun asks God to cover what's wrong and hold us anyway. Today's word.
Your line: best of the merciful. Today, when someone makes a small mistake near you, try covering it rather than pointing at it. Day four hundred ninety-one.

howItsDone: Many Muslims memorize 23:118 and repeat it as a short supplication, often counting it on their fingers or prayer beads after the daily prayers.

fork.setup: the surah opened with 'successful are the believers', then went through a dark scene of people begging to be sent back. how does it end?
options: with a short prayer: forgive and have mercy.
fork.reveal: a short prayer the Prophet is told to say: my Lord, forgive and have mercy, You are the best of the merciful.

original.note: Arabic: my Lord, forgive and have mercy, from 23:118.

trapdoor: what you thought: one request said twice.
what it means: two requests, cover my fault and hold me in mercy, with the reason: You are the best of the merciful.
what a scholar hears: the surah's ring: qad aflaha (23:1) and la yuflihu (23:117); khayru r-rahimin here, arhamu r-rahimin in Ayyub's call (21:83).

sources.quoted: And (O Muhammad) say: My Lord! Forgive and have mercy, for Thou art Best of all who show mercy.

notes: Pickthall wording of 23:118 quoted from memory; please confirm exactly.
Ghafara as 'covering' is the standard lexical sense; the link of rahma to rahim (womb) is widely taught and supported by a hadith qudsi; confirm the framing 'many scholars connect it'.
'Ayyub, nine days ago': Ayyub's call was day 482, nine days before 491.
